title: A joint timing and velocity fit gives a 50.6-degree mutual inclination for TYC 9179-1083-1 under one bright-tertiary geometry
abstract: We fit one Newtonian triple state to 153 published TESS eclipse times, eight published stellar velocities, and eight shape constraints for TYC 9179-1083-1. We use a bright-tertiary shape with TESS third light 0.7849. A local fit gives inner masses of 0.779 and 0.591 solar masses, tertiary mass 1.148 solar masses, outer period 2138.3 days, outer eccentricity 0.0933 and mutual inclination 50.60 degrees. Its weighted loss is 140.51, with 138.12 from times and 1.78 from velocities. This supplies a common timing and velocity state after spectra rejected the masses and geometry used by the earlier timing fit. Doubling the adopted velocity errors changes the masses by less than four percent. IAS15 changes fitted eclipse times by at most 1.94 seconds and velocities by less than 0.04 m/s. No new observations are used. The fit does not search all orbital branches or model individual flux samples. Shape weights and shared data errors prevent a calibrated significance claim. Local mass intervals are conditional estimates. Code, fitted states, source hashes and a verified retrieval script permit reproduction outside the signed package.
